=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- File: .claude/commands/claude-issue-pickup.md
  Line or code reference: line 41 cleanup paragraph ("The pickup left behind reads no queue item, so no target gets two sessions")
  Problem: The claim that the old pickup left behind never reads the queue is too absolute. In `start --restart` mode, the new pickup creates its trigger and reads the queue immediately (step 2). If the old pickup is mid-wake when the restart happens (already past the step 1 trigger check), it continues to read the queue. Both pickups could see the same open item before either closes it, because `claude_issue_route.py queue-pending` is read-only and does not claim items. The `created_at` stand-down check in `-- wake.` mode only applies on the old pickup's next hourly wake, not during its current wake.
  Why it fails at runtime: Two pickups could start duplicate Opus sessions for the same target item. This requires the old pickup to be mid-wake when a `start --restart` with a denied delete occurs, making it a narrow window, but the prose claim of "no target gets two sessions" is not strictly true during that window.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3

- File: tests/test_implement_issue_claude_command.py
  Line or code reference: line ~346 — `keep_one = pickup_cmd[pickup_cmd.index("**Keep exactly one pickup.**"):pickup_cmd.index("**Read the queue.**")]`

The actual heading text in step 1's bullet group (covering the `start`, `— wake.`, `stop` modes and the Cleanup calls paragraph) is something like "**Keep the pickup's trigger correct.**" — not the anchor string. `pickup_cmd.index("**Keep exactly one pickup.**")` raises `ValueError` before any assertion runs, so pytest reports this test as an error, not a clean assertion failure. The test exists specifically to lock in the §26.I pickup restart rule (AD-9); failing at the slice means none of its assertions (cleanup-calls paragraph, `created_at` stand-down, Rules bullet text) ever execute, so the contract test the PR claims to add is in fact non-functional.
  Why it fails at runtime: Every pytest run that imports this module and collects this test will hit the ValueError on the first statement. The test cannot pass on the real tree, on a scratch copy with the diff applied, or in any environment where the pickup file's section header is unchanged from upstream.

- File: .claude/commands/claude-issue-pickup.mdLine or code reference: lines 41–43 (Cleanup calls paragraph) read: "in `start` mode create this session's trigger anyway, and in `— wake.` mode read the queue anyway. The pickup left behind reads no queue item, so no target gets two sessions: its trigger is older than this session's, each of its wakes ends at the `created_at` check in `— wake.` mode, and a later wake of this session deletes it."; CLAUDE.md §26.I (new) reads: "Never retry a cleanup call. When one is denied (by the Auto-mode classifier, a permission rule, or a hook), do not repeat it or reach the same result with another call."
  Problem: The two passages directly contradict each other. §26.I forbids repeating a denied `delete_trigger`, but the Cleanup calls paragraph's mitigation depends on "a later wake of this session deletes it" — which is, by definition, a later attempt at the same denied cleanup. If the delete was permanently denied by the Auto-mode classifier (the very condition §26.I is designed to handle), the rule §26.I itself blocks the cleanup path the paragraph promises will save the situation. The older pickup's hourly trigger therefore remains live indefinitely, and every subsequent wake of the newer pickup tries the same delete and is skipped again. The structural deadlock means the old trigger is removed only by some external event (the user running `stop`, an operator manually intervening, or the older pickup's next hourly wake applying its own `created_at` stand-down).
  Why it fails at runtime: In a `start — restart` whose `delete_trigger` is denied by the Auto-mode classifier (the exact scenario §26.I was authored for, per the issue #5068 incident), the new pickup creates its hourly trigger and reads the queue immediately, while the old pickup's trigger is still alive. Both pickups then wake hourly. Both call `claude_issue_route.py queue-pending` (no in-flight marking, read-only). Both can dispatch `create_session` + `create_trigger` for the same open queue item before either closes it, because `queue_pending` does not lock or claim items and the queue is only closed after a successful session-start. Each subsequent wake of the new pickup re-attempts the same denied delete and is skipped, so the older trigger cannot be removed by the §26.I-cleanup path the paragraph relies on.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- File: .claude/commands/claude-issue-pickup.md; scripts/claude_issue_route.py
  Line or code reference: pickup Cleanup calls paragraph (lines 41–43) and `— wake.` mode entry (lines 38–40); `queue_pending` returns open queue items without claiming them, and the per-item dispatch path closes the queue issue only after `create_session` + `create_trigger` succeed.
  Problem: When §26.I's skip-on-denial rule fires during a `start — restart`, the new pickup proceeds to read the queue and dispatch items even though the old pickup's hourly trigger is still enabled. There is no distributed lock, leader election, or claim-before-dispatch primitive between the two pickups; `claude_issue_route.py queue-pending` is a read that returns every open item regardless of whether another pickup is already processing it, and the queue entry is closed only after a per-item session-start succeeds. The PR's only mitigation is the `created_at` stand-down in `— wake.` mode, which (a) does not apply to the new pickup's actions during its own `start` wake, and (b) per the §26.I contradiction above, can never delete the old trigger if the original delete was denied. The race window is therefore unbounded for as long as the classifier keeps refusing: any two consecutive hourly wakes can read the same still-open queue item and both dispatch `create_session` for the same target.
  Why it fails at runtime: Two concurrent pickups (the original `session_A` whose `delete_trigger` was denied, and the `session_B` started by `start — restart`) both wake on the same hourly cron and both run `queue-pending` before either has a chance to close the items it dispatches. Each then calls `create_session` for the same issue or PR-fix entry, producing two Opus sessions for one target. The downstream `claude-issue-dispatch.md` step 2 path then closes the queue item on success, but only after the session is created — by which time the duplicate session has already been launched and is burning LLM spend on the same target. The §26.I rule explicitly forbids the cleanup retry that would let the new pickup catch up, so the duplication persists across wakes.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

  Line or code reference: pickup "Cleanup calls" paragraph says denied `delete_trigger` "is skipped and noted"; the §26.C step 5 "Terminal, fixer gone" fallback in CLAUDE.md and `implement-plan-claude.md` hand-back step 1 say `delete_trigger` is skipped "only when `get_trigger` … shows its `name` is … `persistent_session_id` is …"; §26.I itself says "not found → already done; skip the delete" and "Any other failure is recorded as `cleanup skipped: <tool> failed (<error>)` and is not retried either; only a denial skips the rest of the step."
  Problem: The §26.I rule distinguishes three outcomes for a targeted cleanup: (a) not-found → skip silently, (b) denied → skip the rest of the step and the remaining cleanups, (c) any other error → record as failed, do not retry.
